claims.statement: Citation verification of the AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN CONVENTION CAVEAT (schemas/af_scc_c0_vacuum.yaml line 99, canonical sha256 1bb78ce9b3572cdac229ad7623ce96908bf4f08dc62c3c6264d97b17c0355508): its cited pointer arXiv:1901.07996 (Grant-Kunzinger-Saemann-Steinbauer, 'The future is not always open', Lett. Math. Phys. 2019, DOI 10.1007/s11005-019-01213-8) SUPPORTS the caveat's factual core at full-text level: chronological futures for continuous (alpha-Holder, 0<alpha<1) metrics may be non-open (Example 3.1, source line 720) and may differ between the smooth/piecewise-C^1 and locally-Lipschitz/absolutely-continuous curve classes (abstract; source lines 190-191; Lemma 2.2, source lines 340-352). The schema's remedy sentence -- 'if the causal relation is degenerate, the witness must instead be a timelike curve from iota(M) to a point of int(M' minus iota(M))' -- is NOT supported by the source: the only openness guarantee the source proves is for the locally-uniformly-timelike / piecewise-C^1 class (Lemma 2.2), and source line 819 shows the pathologies persist even when C^1 curves with finitely many null-tangent points are admitted, so an unqualified 'timelike curve' witness is not class-determined for a merely continuous metric. Verdict PARTIAL; the schema should either pin clause (f)'s degenerate-case witness to the l.u.t./piecewise-C^1 class with a named degeneracy criterion or mark clause (f) an explicit open proof obligation. This claim does NOT assert that the C0 class is open/closed as a theorem, does not resolve clause (f), and does not mark the citation VERIFIED.

claims.statement: The published N0 order-2 evidence (numerics/tests/n0_order_4rung.json#c88146a1375c, class AF-WCC-SCALAR-SPH) is reproduced by an independent from-scratch discretisation that shares none of the published module's r*phi-reduction, Dirichlet-origin, Taylor-start or leapfrog axes. A direct cell-centred finite-volume solve of the unreduced spherical equation phi_tt = phi_rr + (2/r)phi_r with DOP853 (rtol 1e-12, no Taylor bootstrap) measures fit order 1.998947 +/- 0.001163 over dr = 0.2,0.1,0.05,0.025 (pair orders 1.997511, 1.999356, 1.999837; monotone); a same-variable u = r*phi method-of-lines control measures 1.999936 +/- 0.000077; both R5-agree with all three published schemes (lffd 1.996625, cnfd 1.995351, cnfem 1.988860; max |dp| 0.010087 <= R5 bound max(0.25, sqrt(da^2+db^2))). Controls pass: a first-order upwind discretisation is measured at order 0.886 (the norm+fit machinery is discriminative), exact-injection error is exactly 0, refining rtol 100x moves the finest-rung error by 1.1e-10 relative (temporal error negligible), and a different pulse member (r0=9.0, sigma=1.2) measures 1.997752 +/- 0.002460.

hard_failures: HF-06 (critical; nearest code, the A0 taxonomy has no internal-contradiction code): quantifiers.formal lines 54-55 read 'not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M' and D5 lines 79-81 defines q by 'gamma([0,T)) is contained in the causal past J^-(q)'. That is whole-curve single-q containment, which contradicts the class's own canonical predicate at visibility.definition lines 219-220 (single-q TAIL: exists q AND t0 with gamma([t0,T)) contained in J^-(q)) and contradicts quantifiers.negation line 88, which negates the tail predicate. The expansion is strictly weaker: the schema's own example at line 220 (geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region) has a visible tail while the whole curve is not contained in any J^-(q), so it satisfies lines 54-55 but violates the canonical conclusion at line 251. quantifiers.formal and quantifiers.negation are therefore not exact negations of each other, and the class as formally expanded is not equivalent to the F0 AF-WCC-VAC-GEN conclusion object. The canonical gate returns PASS with failed_rules=[] at this hash because R03/R10 check domain resolution and field presence, never agreement with visibility.definition.

HF-06 (major; nearest code, dangling-symbol): conclusion.statement_formal line 251 uses AF_{I+}(M_D), which no leaf of the document defines (grep AF_{I+} matches line 251 only; i_plus.definition line 200 names the concept in prose, and quantifiers D3 line 74 gives the completion) and complete(I+_D), which is defined prose-only at i_plus.completeness_definition line 202. The class is declared bound to statement_formal at line 255, so its equivalence to the F0 text 'the MGHD admits a conformal completion with a complete future null infinity I+' is currently a reader's reconstruction, not a checkable identity.

findings: F-01 HARD (P3; HF-06 class, independently reproduced at the pinned hash): the exact quantifier prefix and the conclusion block expand DIFFERENT visibility predicates. quantifiers.formal (schemas/af_wcc_vacuum.yaml:54-55) closes with 'not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M' and quantifiers.domains.D5 (:79-81) defines q by 'gamma([0,T)) is contained in the causal past J^-(q)' - both are WHOLE-CURVE single-q containment. The class's one canonical predicate, visibility.definition (:219-220), is the single-q TAIL predicate ('exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q)'), and conclusion.statement_formal (:251) binds that predicate by name. Direction: whole-curve non-containment A is IMPLIED by tail non-containment B (a tail is a subset of the curve), so A is strictly weaker than the conclusion's negation; a development with a visible tail but no visible whole curve satisfies the formal expansion and violates the conclusion. The schema itself states the whole-curve reading 'would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region' (:220) and that single-q non-containment must not be replaced by B-containment (:227); class_identity_variants (:231-244) declares exactly ONE canonical predicate. quantifiers.negation (:85-88) negates the TAIL predicate, so quantifiers.formal and quantifiers.negation are not exact negations of each other. Probe P3 fail. Falsifier: state the tail form (with explicit t0) in quantifiers.formal and D5, which also restores formal/negation exactness.

F-02 HARD (P4): D0, the domain of the first quantifier, is a disjunction ('Sobolev variant s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1), or the smooth-with-decay default', :65) while the binder is the pair (s,delta) and the quantified objects are pair-indexed (G_{s,delta}, X^{s,delta}_vac in quantifiers.formal; X^{s,delta}_vac in genericity.ambient_space). J^-(q)') use whole-curve single-q non-containment, and quantifiers.ordered (56-62) binds no t0. visibility.definition (line 220) defines visibility with the tail ('exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q)') and visibility.negation_conclusion (line 222) is the matching tail negation ('for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail ... is NOT contained'). Since whole-curve containment A(q) implies tail containment B(q,t0) and not conversely, 'not exists q A(q)' is STRICTLY WEAKER than 'not exists q exists t0 B(q,t0)'. quantifiers.negation (84-88) negates the tail predicate ('some ... geodesic ... is visible from I+'), so the formal block and its declared negation are not complements of each other.
